title: Coordination Matters: Process-Aware Evaluation of Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2605.06557v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) benchmarks commonly emphasize aggregate outcomes such as return, success rate, or completion time. While essential, these metrics can obscure how agents coordinate and fail to distinguish policies that achieve similar outcomes through different interaction processes. We propose a process-aware evaluation framework that complements aggregate performance with diagnostics of interference, coordinated task completion, participation, and coordination efficiency. We evaluate the framework in STAT, a controlled spatial task-allocation testbed, and examine its broader applicability in two established cooperative MARL benchmarks. Across diverse value-based and actor-critic methods, we find policies with nearly identical return can exhibit substantial differences in coordination behavior. translated_title: 协同至关重要：面向协作式多智能体强化学习的过程感知评估
translated_abstract: 协作式多智能体强化学习（MARL）基准测试通常强调回报、成功率或完成时间等聚合性结果。虽然这些指标至关重要，但它们可能掩盖智能体之间如何进行协调，并且无法区分通过不同交互过程达到相似结果的策略。我们提出了一个过程感知的评估框架，通过干扰、协同任务完成、参与度和协调效率等诊断指标来补充聚合性能的评估。我们在STAT——一个受控的空间任务分配测试平台——中评估了该框架，并检验了其在两个成熟的协作式MARL基准测试中更广泛的适用性。在多种基于价值和演员-评论家的方法中，我们发现回报几乎相同的策略在协调行为上可能存在显著差异。STAT中的受控规模扩展实验揭示了空间、任务和智能体规模扩展各自不同的过程特征。
tldr: 本文提出了一个过程感知的多智能体强化学习评估框架，通过干扰、协同任务完成、参与度和协调效率等诊断指标补充传统聚合性能指标，揭示了回报相近的策略在协调行为上可能存在显著差异。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a process-aware evaluation framework for cooperative MARL that complements aggregate performance with diagnostics of interference, coordinated task completion, participation, and coordination efficiency, revealing that policies with nearly identical returns can exhibit substantially different coordination behaviors.
